relevance.rationale: Two corpus blocks rest on a Plancherel central limit theorem and neither cites one. conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit states 'the Kerov q-hook walk and the Feray-Meliot q-Plancherel Central Limit Theorem ensure O(1/sqrt(k)) convergence' with cites: [feray2010, kerov1996]; prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2) states 'character fluctuations have variance O(1/sqrt(n-3))' citing feray2010 alone. But feray2010 in references.ts is 'Stanley's formula for characters of the symmetric group' (Annals of Combinatorics 13, 2010) — a character-formula paper, NOT a central limit theorem, and not the Feray-Meliot q-Plancherel asymptotics paper the prose names. This document is the canonical complete proof of the q = 1 statement those blocks are deforming, written by Kerov's collaborators from his notes. It is the result the corpus's q-deformed claims are the deformation of, and the current citation does not support the claim made. Flagging the mis-citation is itself a finding.

keyResults.statement: Kerov's CLT: for lambda drawn from Plancherel measure M_n, the rescaled boundary satisfies n^{-1/2} lambda(sqrt(n) x) ~ Omega(x) + (2/sqrt(n)) Delta(x), with Omega(x) = (2/pi)(x arcsin(x/2) + sqrt(4 - x^2)) on |x| <= 2 and Delta a generalized Gaussian process given by the random trigonometric series Delta(2 cos theta) = (1/pi) sum_{k>=2} (xi_k/sqrt(k)) sin(k theta), xi_k i.i.d. standard normal.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the actual q = 1 fluctuation theorem — including the exact 1/sqrt(n) scale — that conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit's O(1/sqrt(k)) claim and prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2) are asserting a q-analogue of. Replaces a citation (feray2010) that does not state a CLT.

keyResults.statement: Central limit theorem for normalized character values on cycles: character ratios evaluated on cycles of different lengths are asymptotically independent Gaussians with explicit variances.
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the precise q = 1 form of prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2)'s 'character fluctuations have variance O(...)'; the asymptotic independence across cycle lengths is additional structure the corpus block does not currently record and which any q-deformed statement would have to reproduce or break.

keyResults.locator: §10 (free cumulants and Biane's theorem); §3-§4 (the p#_k basis and filtrations in A)
keyResults.statement: The proof is organised through the algebra of polynomial functions on Young diagrams, the elements p#_k, and free cumulants, connecting to Biane's asymptotic character theory.
keyResults.useForFolio: rem:non-commutative-probability-dictionary already frames the Hecke GNS data in free-probability terms; §10 gives the bridge between the Plancherel CLT and the free-cumulant language the corpus uses, so a q-deformed statement can be posed in the corpus's own coordinates.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; no Ivanov or Olshanski entry in references.ts.
prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2) cites feray2010 ('Stanley's formula for characters') for a fluctuation/variance claim that paper does not make; the q = 1 CLT source belongs here.

conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit's prose names a 'Feray-Meliot q-Plancherel Central Limit Theorem' but cites feray2010 + kerov1996; the named q-CLT paper is absent from references.ts and the q = 1 antecedent is uncited. Add this and verify the Feray-Meliot citation separately.

entry.note: Source IS held: library/arxiv-math-0304010v1. The ledger recorded it as unavailable, so corpus-grep path 5 reported the repo does not have it — which sends an agent to re-derive a result it could have cited. Re-pointed from the measurement in scripts/cited-source-availability-audit.py.
